text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
IgaSwiathek(x) ::: x is Iga Świątek.
RolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
Female(x) ::: x is female.
Male(x) ::: x is male.
CocoGauff(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.
AtTournament(x, y) ::: x was at tournament y.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly, then they are among the most active players.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaSwiathek) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly.
∀x (AtTournament(x, RolandGaron2022) ∧ Female(x)) → LostTo(x, IgaSwiathek) ::: All female players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtTournament(x, RolandGaron2022) ∧ Male(x)) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal) ::: All male players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
∀x (CocoGauff(x) ∧ (RankedHighly(x) ∨ LostTo(x, RafaelNadal))) → ¬Male(x) ::: If Coco Gauff is highly ranked or lost to Rafael Nadal, then she is not male.
AtTournament(CocoGauff, RolandGaron2022) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
∀x (CocoGauff(x)) → ActivePlayer(x) ::: Coco Gauff is among the most active major tennis players.
